structured.name: Antigua and Barbuda
structured._source: wikidata (CC0); landBorders + naturalResources from CIA World Factbook (public domain)

prose.hook: Antigua and Barbuda sits in the Caribbean between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic, east-southeast of Puerto Rico, with no land borders to speak of since it is made up entirely of islands. Antigua's deeply indented shoreline gives it many natural harbors and beaches, while Barbuda has a large western harbor of its own. The pleasant climate has made tourism the country's defining pursuit, and even its exports run to an eclectic mix including ships and paintings alongside refined petroleum and shellfish.
prose.physicalGeography: The islands are mostly low-lying limestone and coral formations, with some higher volcanic terrain rising above them. Antigua's coastline is deeply indented, producing numerous natural harbors and beaches, while Barbuda's most notable feature is its large western harbor.
prose.climate: The climate is tropical maritime, with little variation in temperature across the seasons. Hurricanes and tropical storms are a recurring feature from July to October, and the islands also experience periodic droughts.
prose.economy: Tourism and construction drive the economy, alongside an emerging focus on the so-called blue economy. A limited water supply and vulnerability to hurricanes constrain economic activity, though improving road infrastructure and a welcoming stance toward foreign direct investment support growth, and the country has been exploring financial innovation through cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Beyond tourism and construction, light manufacturing produces clothing, alcohol, and household appliances, while exports include refined petroleum, ships, soybean meal, shellfish, and paintings.
prose.peopleAndCulture: English is the official language, alongside Antiguan Creole, an English-based creole. The population is predominantly Protestant, with Anglicans forming the largest single group alongside Seventh Day Adventists, Pentecostals, and several other denominations, plus a smaller Roman Catholic community. Most residents are of African descent, with smaller shares of mixed, Hispanic, and White heritage.
